title: Disa in Chad people group profile | Joshua Project
text: The Disa people speak a language from the Nilo-Saharan family, which connects them to other ethnic groups in the Sahel region. Their history is rooted in the savanna and semi-arid zones of Chad, where they have lived for generations as part of small, rural communities.

title: Disa language — Grokipedia
text: Disa is a minor, endangered language spoken primarily by the Disa people in the Guéra region of central Chad, particularly in the Chinguil subprefecture.
